blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Predicting spatial gene expression from standard H&E images could extend molecular analysis to tissues without spatial transcriptomic measurements. A standard Transformer applies self-attention over spots but ignores where each spot sits in the tissue, whereas a spot's molecular state depends on tissue context at multiple spatial scales. Building on this insight, we introduce MIST, a Multi-context Spatial Transformer that augments the self-attention backbone with two context pathways applied in every layer: a coordinate-invariant local pathway that attends over spatial k-nearest-neighbor spots, and a slide pathway that broadcasts a whole-slide summary to every spot; the model predicts all spots in a single forward pass. Because coordinates enter only through pairwise distances, the local pathway is invariant to translations, rotations, and reflections when image features are fixed. In intra-cohort evaluation across six human organ cohorts from HEST-1k, MIST improves mean Pearson correlation over the strongest evaluated baseline by 9.7%, 11.6%, and 11.4% for 10-, 50-, and 100-gene panels, respectively, with the lowest average MSE and MAE. MIST further improves leave-one-organ-out transfer by 6.0% over the next strongest baseline, attains the best expression-derived domain recovery (highest mean ARI and NMI at every clustering resolution, and higher NMI than the closest baseline on 84% of held-out slides), and reproduces spatial expression patterns of selected cancer-marker genes. Together, these results show that adding local and slide context to a vanilla Transformer backbone is an effective approach to spatial gene expression prediction from histology.

blocks.en: 4.1 RQ1: Predictive performance across diverse organs
blocks.zh: 4.1 RQ1:不同机关的预测业绩

blocks.en: We first ask whether MIST consistently predicts gene expression across diverse organs. For a fair comparison, all methods use frozen UNI+CONCH features with matched gene panels and data splits.
blocks.zh: 我们首先问,MIST是否始终如一地预测不同器官的基因表达。 为了进行公平的比较,所有方法都使用冷冻的UNI+CONCH特性,并配对基因板和数据分割.

blocks.en: We begin with within-organ evaluation , where each model is trained and tested within the same organ. Across the 50-gene HVG, DEG, and HMHVG panels, MIST achieves mean PCCs of 0.496 0.496 , 0.615 0.615 , and 0.650 0.650 , respectively, compared with BLEEP’s 0.444 0.444 , 0.559 0.559 , and 0.587 0.587 (Table 1 ). Across HVG panel sizes, MIST reaches PCC@10/50/100 of 0.600 / 0.496 / 0.559 0.600/0.496/0.559 , leading all six cohorts at PCC@50 with an 11.6 % 11.6\% cohort-averaged gain over BLEEP; the 10- and 100-gene panel results are in Appendix F (Table 7 ). It also achieves the lowest average MSE and MAE across all evaluated panel strategies and sizes.
blocks.zh: 我们从机构内部评价开始, 在50种HVG、DEG和HMHVG小组中,MIST的平均PCC分别为0.496 0.496、0.615 0.615和0.650 0.650,而BLEEP的0.444 0.44、0.559 0.559和0.587 0587(表1)。 在整个HVG小组规模中,MIST达到PCC@10/50/100(0.600/0.496/0.559/0.496/0.559),在PCC@50中领导所有6个组别,比BLEEP的平均收益率为11.6%;10个组和100个组别的结果见附录F(表7)。 它还在所有评估的小组战略和规模中实现了最低的平均MSE和MAE。

blocks.en: The improvement is consistent across runs. Treating each cohort–seed run as the statistical unit ( n = 18 n{=}18 ), MIST improves PCC@50 over BLEEP by 0.051 0.051 (95% bootstrap CI [ 0.041 , 0.062 ] [0.041,0.062] ; Wilcoxon p = 7.6 × 10 − 6 p=7.6\times 10^{-6} ). At the gene level, MIST also achieves higher PCC than BLEEP for 87 % 87\% of the 300 evaluated genes; we report this descriptively because genes within a slide are correlated. Statistical details are provided in Appendix E .

blocks.en: Finally, in the pooled multi-organ setting , a single MIST model is trained jointly across all six organs using a shared 14-gene leakage-safe panel. It achieves the highest mean PCC ( 0.599 0.599 ), compared with BLEEP ( 0.587 0.587 ) and Hist2ST ( 0.556 0.556 ) (Table 2 ). Together, these results show consistent gains both within individual organs and across a shared multi-organ setting.

blocks.en: 4.2 RQ2: Cross-organ transfer to an unseen organ
blocks.zh: 4.2 RQ2:向看不见的机关的跨器官转移

blocks.en: Having established consistent performance across organs represented during training, we next ask whether MIST can transfer to an entirely unseen organ. We evaluate this using leave-one-organ-out (LOOO) evaluation, where each fold withholds one organ from training and tests exclusively on that organ, ensuring that its anatomy is absent from the training set. As shown in Table 3 , MIST achieves the best mean PCC ( 0.422 0.422 vs. BLEEP 0.398 0.398 ) and matches or exceeds BLEEP on all six held-out organs, with PAAD effectively tied ( 0.499 0.499 vs. 0.497 0.497 ). Across the 18 organ × \times seed runs, this improvement is significant (two-sided Wilcoxon p = 0.018 p{=}0.018 ; Appendix E ), showing that MIST retains consistent gains even when evaluated on organs excluded from training.

With image features fixed, we translate spot coordinates by ( 37.2 , − 91.4 ) (37.2,-91.4) , rotate them by 0.731 0.731 radians, reflect them across the vertical axis, and permute spot order. Across CCRCC, PRAD, and the pooled six-organ setting, these transformations cause only negligible changes in PCC(Table 4 ). Reflection leaves predictions unchanged, while the tiny differences under translation, rotation, and permutation arise from numerical effects in k k NN selection when distances are tied or nearly tied.
blocks.zh: 在前面的一节中,我们显示新增的局部路径和滑行路径可以改善预测;我们接下来测试模型是否稳定地适应坐标框的变化. 固定图像特征后,我们翻译的点座坐标为(37.2,−91.4)(37.2-91.4),旋转的点座坐标为0.731 0.731弧度,在垂直轴上反射,并永久点座顺序. 这些转变在整个《公约》和《公约》以及六组织集合环境中只造成微小的变化(表4)。 反射使预测保持不变,而翻译、旋转和演化方面的微小差异则产生于在 k NN 选择中,距离被绑定或接近绑定时的数值效应。

blocks.en: 4.5 RQ5: Spatial structure preservation
blocks.zh: 4.5 RQ5:空间结构保护

blocks.en: So far, we have shown that MIST predicts gene expression accurately. We next ask whether it also preserves spatial tissue structure. We cluster spots into k = 6 k{=}6 domains using KMeans, separately from predicted and measured expression, and compare the resulting partitions using ARI and NMI on held-out slides (Figure 3 ).

This ordering remains unchanged for k ∈ 4 , 6 , 8 , 10 k\in{4,6,8,10} (Appendix I ). These results indicate that MIST better preserves spatial gene expression structure, particularly according to NMI.

blocks.en: 4.6 Case Study: Recovering Cancer-Marker Genes
blocks.zh: 4.6 案例研究:恢复癌症-马克基因

blocks.en: To further test its biological relevance, we ask whether MIST can recover canonical cancer-marker genes. We focus on established markers for melanoma (SKCM) Ohsie et al. (2008) and breast cancer (IDC), the latter including the clinically used HER2, ER, and PR receptor markers Wolff et al. (2018) ; Allison et al. (2020) . Because several markers are outside the default panel, we evaluate them using the 200-gene panel and measure the Pearson correlation between predicted and measured expression for each gene (Figure 5 ).
blocks.zh: 为了进一步测试其生物学相关性,我们询问MIST是否能够恢复犬类癌症标记基因. 我们专注于黑色素瘤的既定标记(SKCM) Ohsie等人(2008年)和乳腺癌(IDC),后者包括临床上使用的HER2,ER和PR受体标记Wolff等人(2018年);Allison等人(2020年). 由于数个标记都位于默认面板之外,所以我们使用200基因面板来评价它们,并测量每个基因的预测和测量表达值之间的皮尔逊相关性(图5 ).

blocks.en: MIST achieves high correlation for melanoma markers (mean 0.895 0.895 ; MLANA 0.949 0.949 ) and good correlation for breast-cancer markers (mean 0.717 0.717 ; HER2 0.829 0.829 ). It obtains the highest average correlation for both cancers, with the top score for all melanoma markers and five of seven breast-cancer markers. Moreover, its predicted maps closely match the measured tumor layout (Figure 6 , r ≥ 0.91 r\geq 0.91 ).
blocks.zh: MIST对黑色素瘤标记(平均0.895 0.895;MLANA 0.949 0.949)具有高度相关性,对乳腺癌标记(平均0.717 0.717;HER2 0.829 0.829)具有良好的相关性。 它获得两种癌症中最高的平均相关性,所有黑色素瘤标记的得分最高,7个乳腺癌标记的得分最高. 此外,其预测地图与测量的肿瘤布局非常吻合(图6,r 0.91 r\ geq 0.91 )。

blocks.en: Together, these results show that MIST can recover both the expression and spatial patterns of several canonical cancer markers from H&E. We interpret this as improved marker-gene prediction, not as evidence of standalone clinical utility.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 6. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en:
We introduced MIST , which augments a self-attention backbone with
local spatial-neighborhood attention and slide-level context for gene
expression prediction from histology. Across six HEST-1k organ cohorts, MIST improves predictive performance, while ablations show that the gains
come from the added local and slide pathways and from using spatially defined
neighbors. The model also improves held-out-organ transfer and better preserves
expression-derived spatial structure. Generalization to unseen organs remains challenging. Future work will explore
slide-level metadata, transcriptome-wide prediction, end-to-end image encoding,
and predictive uncertainty to improve robustness and generalization.

We use frozen UNI (ViT-L/16, 1,024-dimensional image embeddings; Hugging Face model card ) Chen et al. (2024b) and
CONCH (ViT-B/16, 512-dimensional image embeddings; Hugging Face model card ) Lu et al. (2024) .
Both encoders were evaluated for gene expression prediction in the HEST-1k benchmark Jaume et al. (2024) . We test UNI and CONCH separately and concatenate their features to obtain
1,536-dimensional spot embeddings. Concatenation gives the highest mean PCC in our encoder
comparison: 0.496, compared with 0.484 for UNI and 0.463 for CONCH alone (Table 7 ;
Appendix 8 ). We therefore use UNI+CONCH in the main comparisons.

blocks.en:
Intra-cohort training fits a model within each cohort. Pooled five-fold validation trains across
organs while holding out slide-level samples; organ identity defines the protocol but is not a model
input. LOOO trains on all-but-one organ and tests the held-out organ. We report PCC, MSE, MAE, and
(for domain recovery) ARI and NMI, averaged over outer folds and three seeds. Checkpoints are selected on inner validation and evaluated
once on the outer test fold; single-slide folds use disjoint spots for inner validation. Patient-level
disjointness is not guaranteed where identifiers are unavailable.

We compare with ST-Net He et al. (2020) , Hist2ST Zeng et al. (2022) , BLEEP Xie et al. (2023) ,
and STEM Zhu et al. (2025) under matched features, panels, splits, budgets, and checkpoint

To evaluate MIST , we use six cohorts from the HEST-1k dataset Jaume et al. (2024) , a curated

(2) IDC (breast) provides 4 WSIs and 44,974 spots;
(3) PRAD (prostate) provides 23 WSIs and 62,710 spots;

(5) LUNG provides 2 WSIs and 7,505 spots; and

Spots are counted after barcode filtering; all cohorts use Visium spots with a 55 µm diameter.

resolution, and the log ⁡ ( 1 + x ) \log(1+x) -transformed expression over the selected gene panel as the prediction
target. Per-cohort sample, spot, and cross-validation-fold counts are summarized in
Table 5 .

blocks.en:
Each “sample” in Table 5 is a distinct HEST-1k slide (a whole-slide section),
and every fold is slide-disjoint : no slide is shared between training and test, the pooled
regime holds out entire slides, and the leave-one-organ-out regime holds out entire organs. HEST-1k
patient/donor identifiers are not distributed with the per-slide data in our pipeline, so for a cohort
in which one donor may contribute several slides we cannot verify patient-level disjointness. The
intra-cohort and pooled numbers should therefore be read as slide-level generalization and
could be optimistic if a cohort mixes multiple slides from the same patient; this risk is largest for
the two multi-slide cohorts, CCRCC (24 slides) and PRAD (23 slides), and small for the remaining
cohorts (IDC 4, PAAD 3, LUNG 2, SKCM 2 slides). Importantly, the cross-organ LOOO transfer results
(our central generalization claim) are unaffected, because an entire organ (and hence a disjoint set
of patients) is withheld at test time.
